investigation: AC strong identity path (GTIN/MPN/Model vs. series_or_platform) — global verification + internal data-availability audit. NO shadow test, NO pilot run — gated before that stage, per the mission's own stop conditions.

global_research.method: External research fork, primary sources only where reachable (session WebSearch budget already exhausted from prior missions this day; worked around via direct WebFetch, several sources 403/404/blocked)
global_research.A_gtin: CONFIRMED (Wikipedia/GS1-derived): GTIN identifies a specific trade item at variant/packaging level, registry-backed. One caveat found: no worldwide consensus on the GTIN-14 indicator digit's packaging-level meaning — a real, sourced ambiguity even within the standard.
global_research.B_google_merchant_CORRECTION: This is the load-bearing finding. Google's own Merchant Center help page (support.google.com/merchants/answer/160161, fetched directly) does NOT say 'Brand+MPN can clearly specify one product' the way the founder's framing implied. GTIN is the primary, strongly-recommended identifier; Brand+MPN are supplementary, offered only 'if available', with an explicit warning: 'Don't make up, guess, or include values from similar products.' That warning is itself evidence Google does not treat MPN as verified/certified the way GTIN is (GTIN has a real GS1 registry; MPN has none).
global_research.C_through_G: UNVERIFIED this session — primary sources for Model-vs-MPN distinction, Amazon's Parent/Child ASIN docs, HVAC split-system model conventions, and MPN-collision entity-resolution literature were blocked, 404, or not reached given the exhausted search budget. Treated as prior general knowledge, NOT confirmed fact, and flagged as a residual unknown.
global_research.GLOBAL_PRINCIPLE: PARTIAL — GTIN's strength is confirmed; the founder's specific claim about Google's guidance for Brand+MPN is corrected (weaker, unverified, not co-equal with GTIN). This argues for keeping any MPN-based path's conflict-gate and independent-verification requirements strict, not for loosening series_or_platform on the strength of MPN alone.

adr_077_reconstruction.what_actually_happened: lg|split|NO_SERIES|18000 merged three genuinely different LG design lines — Art Cool (premium), Fresh DV, AirFit — at the same BTU, price spread 1,650 to 5,280 SAR (3.2x). Root cause: all three shared brand+type+BTU+tech+mode with no series distinction captured, so they collapsed into one NO_SERIES bucket and corroborated as 'the same product.'
adr_077_reconstruction.the_fix: extracted the three design-line NAMES as series_or_platform values (a marketing-name discriminator), creating 8 correct distinct canonicals. Never used model/MPN at all.
adr_077_reconstruction.explicitly_tried_and_reverted: Flipping AC to requireValidTier:true (dropping ALL NO_SERIES corroboration globally) was tried and reverted — the audit found MOST NO_SERIES AC merges are legitimate (budget/window units, low price spread = genuinely the same simple product). This is important, existing, direct evidence that series_or_platform's necessity is NOT uniform across the AC population — it matters most for premium/design-differentiated products, not generic/budget ones.
adr_077_reconstruction.the_residual_deferred_issue_is_the_found: The SAME ADR records a still-open residual: lg|split|NO_SERIES|18000 still holds model-code-only LG variants (NS182xx, 'Smart') separable ONLY by model number — and the ADR states this 'conflicts with cross-store corroboration' because model numbers are 'store-inconsistent' (different stores format/abbreviate them differently). Tawveeri already, once, ran directly into the exact problem a naive Path C (exact Model) implementation would recreate.
adr_077_reconstruction.ADR_077_PROTECTED_BY_STRONG_IDENTIFIER: PARTIAL — a genuinely verified, carefully-normalized MPN/model WOULD have distinguished ArtCool from FreshDV in principle (same discriminating job as series, via a manufacturer code instead of a marketing name). But Tawveeri's own prior, documented experience in this exact ADR shows raw model-number matching, without careful format-normalization, creates real corroboration failures. Not a clean YES. Not a NO that ends the investigation either — a PARTIAL that specifically demands the 'model normalization caution' the mission's own §17 anticipates.

gtin_ean_upc.finding: Present, but negligible. 3 of 3,565 Amazon AC raw_observations rows (0.08%) carry a real 12-digit UPC value (756179351725) — all three are almost certainly the SAME physical product re-scraped on different dates, not three different products. Realistically ~1 unique AC product in the entire Amazon AC catalog has a captured UPC.
gtin_ean_upc.verdict: PATH A (GTIN) fails on data-availability grounds, not on principle. There is no usable GTIN population to build a truth sheet from, let alone shadow-test.

mpn_model_number.finding: No dedicated MPN field exists anywhere in the schema. Real manufacturer model-like strings DO appear in captured Amazon PDP spec text at a low, inconsistent rate — confirmed directly: 'SVPOR16' captured as an 'Item model number' spec value on one real row. Separately, normalized_product_observations.model_number is already sparsely populated for AC (a handful of real values found, e.g. 'AR24DSFZAWK/MG' — a real Samsung WindFree-family model number, matching ADR-077's own cited case) via a PRE-EXISTING, separate 'model-corroboration-v1' writer referenced in ADR-074 — not via the AC plugin itself, and not currently consulted by identity.ts at all.
mpn_model_number.verdict: PATH B/C (MPN/Model) has a real, if thin, foundation to build on — but ZERO dedicated, tested extraction/normalization/uniqueness-verification path exists today. There is nothing to shadow-test; there is only scattered, uncurated raw material.

internal_data_availability_audit.canonical_products_category_correction: A first-pass query used category='ac' against canonical_products and got a false zero — canonical_products actually uses category='air_conditioner' (1,670 rows), matching the storefront layer, NOT the short 'ac' label normalized_product_observations uses. Same layer-naming-mismatch class of bug as ADR-311's original mis-diagnosis. Corrected before this report was written, not left standing.

why_the_shadow_test_and_pilot_were_not_r: Sections 4-15 of the mission (build a 30-50 product truth sheet, measure identifier quality, shadow-test, 5-product live pilot) all depend on having a real, extracted, normalized MPN/GTIN dataset to test against. That dataset does not exist: GTIN covers ~1 product platform-wide: MPN/model exists only as scattered, uncurated raw text with no extraction, normalization, or uniqueness-verification logic built. Running a 'shadow test' against this would not be evaluating a real capability — it would be evaluating almost-empty data, which cannot satisfy the mission's own explicit gate ('identifiers independently verified... shadow test clean' as preconditions for even a 5-product pilot). Per the mission's own §0/§1 ('if something feels uncertain: STOP', 'do not proceed if the external principle itself fails'), the correct stopping point is here — not because the founder's principle is wrong, but because Tawveeri isn't instrumented to test it yet.
recommended_next_safest_step_not_execute: Build a narrow, tested, provenance-aware MPN/model extractor — the same rigor and pattern as scripts/tps-plugins/ac/pdp-evidence.ts (ADR-315): a new, standalone, unwired module reading the 'Item model number' / 'Manufacturer Reference' spec keys already confirmed to sometimes exist in captured PDP data, with explicit token-preservation (per the mission's own §17 — no aggressive stripping of suffixes/prefixes/regional codes) and uniqueness-verification logic (does the same MPN ever map to >1 distinct product across the sample — a real collision check) BEFORE attempting to build the truth sheet or shadow test this mission's later sections describe. This is itself new engineering requiring its own dry-run/review cycle, not a quick add-on to today's work.
